homelands.place: Pontic-Caspian steppe, north of the Black and Caspian seas
homelands.date: roughly 4,500 to 6,500 years ago (Anthony's c. 4500 to 2500 BCE)
homelands.note: The majority view among linguists and archaeologists, strengthened by ancient DNA showing a large movement of steppe ancestry into Europe about 5,000 years ago.

homelands.date: roughly 8,000 to 9,500 years ago, with the spread of farming (the authors' approximate range)
homelands.note: Links the family's spread to the first farmers; supported by some dated phylogenies, rejected by most specialists because of shared vocabulary for wheels and wagons.

homelands.place: South of the Caucasus (northern Fertile Crescent)
homelands.date: about 8,100 years ago for the first split (the authors' estimate)
homelands.note: A dated phylogeny places the root south of the Caucasus, with a later branch moving onto the steppe.
Widely accepted: all but one of Austronesian's first-order branches are spoken only on Taiwan.
Widely accepted. Bantu is one branch of Atlantic-Congo; the routes of the later spread south and east are debated.

homelands.place: Middle Volga, Kama and the Ural Mountains (approximate)
homelands.date: no single agreed date; a dated phylogeny puts the family's first splits several thousand years ago
homelands.note: One of two contested views: a homeland in the Volga and Kama region west of the Urals.

homelands.place: Western Siberia, the Sayan and upper Yenisei area (approximate)
homelands.date: spread west from about 4,200 years ago
homelands.note: The more recent of the two contested views: a homeland in Siberia, with a spread west to the Volga in the early Metal Age, roughly 4,200 to 3,900 years ago.

homelands.date: about 2,100 years ago for the first split, Bolgar and Common Turkic (95% range 1,500 to 2,800)
homelands.note: Broadly agreed for Proto-Turkic itself; its deeper ancestry and any link to Mongolic or other families are disputed.

homelands.place: Upper and middle Yellow River basin, northern China
homelands.date: roughly 5,900 to 7,200 years ago (the two studies' estimates)
homelands.note: Supported by two dated phylogenies; an alternative places the homeland further south-west, in Sichuan or north-east India.

homelands.place: Horn of Africa and the Red Sea hills
homelands.date: more than 10,000 years ago, by Ehret's reckoning possibly much earlier
homelands.note: Five of the six branches are spoken only in Africa; very old and very uncertain.

homelands.date: more than 10,000 years ago, linked by Militarev to the Natufian
homelands.note: Rests on reconstructed farming words; a minority view.

homelands.place: West Africa, perhaps the inland Niger region
homelands.date: probably more than 10,000 years ago; no agreed date
homelands.note: The most uncertain of all: Glottolog does not accept Niger-Congo as a proven family and lists Atlantic-Congo, Mande, Dogon, Ijoid and others separately.

homelands.place: Gulf Plains of north-west Queensland, Australia
homelands.date: roughly 6,000 years ago (the authors' approximate estimate)
homelands.note: From a dated phylogeography of the family; Pama-Nyungan covers most of Australia.
Argues that Proto-Uto-Aztecan speakers were maize farmers who spread north.

homelands.place: South-western United States, southern Great Basin
homelands.note: Argues from plant and animal names for a homeland of foragers in the south-west United States.

homelands.place: Central coast and highlands of Peru
homelands.note: Broadly agreed: the deepest split, between Quechua I and II, lies in central Peru, far from the later Inca centre at Cusco.
